content.title: Walkthroughs: checked, citation-only reviews of a PR stack, behind an experiment
content.intent: This stack adds Walkthroughs: an API-started agent Turn that writes a structured review of a PR stack, where every citation is re-checked against GitHub before it is stored.

chapters.caption: A model summary of a PR can quote code that does not exist, so the model may only cite.
chapters.body: Reviewers of an agent-written stack get either the raw diff or a summary that can invent code. The Walkthrough format fixes the shape: the model cites PRs, files, line ranges and message seqs, never copies text, and each change type has fixed slots [1].

evidence.note: Contract: cite, never copy; fixed slots per change type

asks: Why not let the model quote code directly?

chapters.caption: A pure validator, diff parser, and excerpt builder decide what may be stored.
chapters.body: validateWalkthrough returns problems: unresolved citations, uncited markers, wrong slots, a cause with no code, and any hunk neither cited nor in not_covered [1]. Mechanical files are dropped before the model sees them and only counted [2]. Excerpts are copied from the provider diff, not from model output [3].
asks: What counts as a mechanical file?
Can a citation point outside the diff?

chapters.caption: Plugins get a read-only codeChanges hook group so core never calls GitHub itself.
chapters.body: Core must not call provider APIs, so 3088 adds an optional codeChanges group: readStack, readDiff and readFile, which return undefined only for missing items [2]. Their context carries plugin egress [1]. Core picks the plugin by provider name and gives it a system Actor whose auth handler never prompts anyone [3].
asks: Which credentials do these reads use?

chapters.caption: GitHub reads the open stack around a PR and diffs exact commits.
chapters.body: readStack asks the Stacks API, falls back to walking base branches, and drops merged or closed layers except the one asked for [1]. The walk stops at the trunk, a fork in the chain, or 10 levels [2][4]. readDiff compares the exact base and head SHAs, so a later push cannot change what is described [3].

decisions.question: The fallback walk matches parents by owner:branch, so a stacked PR whose head is in a fork is not found. Is that acceptable?

asks: What happens when the repo has no Stacks API?

chapters.caption: Each generation gets a version row, and one live version is allowed per snapshot.
chapters.body: Migration 0100 adds junior_walkthrough_versions with a partial unique index: one non-failed version per provider, repository and snapshot key [1][2]. startWalkthroughVersion inserts with onConflictDoNothing and returns the live row on conflict, so a second click joins instead of generating twice [3][4].

decisions.question: generation_conversation_id has no foreign key, so a deleted generation Conversation leaves its version pointing at nothing. Is that fine?

asks: Where does the document itself live?

chapters.caption: The migration only adds a table, but every list query gains one NOT EXISTS probe.
chapters.body: The migration only adds a table and indexes. Its one live effect: listedConversation adds a NOT EXISTS probe on generation_conversation_id to every list and search [1], served by that column's unique index. A test shows a generation Conversation drops out of the list [2]. To roll back, revert code first: the filter needs the table.

decisions.question: The extra probe on every list and search was measured only on a synthetic 100k-row dataset. Is that enough before it ships?

asks: Does this slow the home list?

chapters.caption: submitWalkthrough re-reads every cited fact from trusted sources before it stores anything.
chapters.body: The model explores in its untrusted sandbox, led by a skill hidden from other Turns [1], then calls submitWalkthrough [4]. The tool re-reads diffs and head files through the plugin hooks, rebuilds known URLs and message seqs, and returns validator problems as a tool input error to fix [2]. Messages are copied only after an access check [3].

decisions.question: In this generation, gh and git failed with Missing GITHUB_APP_ID. Nothing checks sandbox GitHub access before a generation Turn starts.

asks: What if the model cites a file it never read?

chapters.caption: Only a generation Turn gets the submit tool, and it cannot reach people or agents.
chapters.body: A new WALKTHROUGH_GENERATION behavior is the only one with submitWalkthrough on. It also turns off agents, the review desk, subscriptions, user customization and noReply [1][2]. The tool is built only when that flag and AgentRun.walkthroughGeneration are both set [3][4], and only the Turn worker sets that field.

evidence.note: submitWalkthrough is false for every other behavior

asks: Could a normal chat Turn call submitWalkthrough?

chapters.caption: A click claims a version, and only the winning click queues one hidden generation Turn.
chapters.body: POST /api/walkthroughs reads the stack, then claims a version [1]. Only the click that wins the claim creates a public web Conversation whose first message is $walkthrough plus the commits; if enqueue fails, the version fails [2]. A version still generating after 30 minutes is failed on the next click for that snapshot [3][4].

decisions.question: The generation Turn runs as the person who clicked, in a public Conversation. Should its sandbox use that person's credentials?

asks: What if two people click at once?
Is the source Conversation always used?

chapters.caption: A generation Turn that completes without a Walkthrough fails its version so a retry can start.
chapters.body: The Turn worker looks up the generating version by Conversation id and passes it into the run [1][2]. When the Turn completes, finish() fails the version unless submitWalkthrough already marked it ready [3]. The thrown-error and cancel paths never call finish(), so those versions wait for the 30-minute reaper [4].

evidence.note: Error and cancel paths; no finish() call

decisions.question: Should a thrown or stopped generation Turn fail its version right away instead of waiting for a click after 30 minutes?

asks: What happens to a Turn that yields and resumes?

chapters.caption: Generation Turns get their own cap of 80 tool calls and $5.
chapters.body: TurnBehavior gains optional limits, and the generation behavior sets 80 tool calls and $5 [1][2]. The agent run reads them and falls back to the app defaults [3], then uses them in the existing limit gate and error messages [4]. Other Turns keep the same limits as before.

decisions.question: The 80-call and $5 caps are not yet backed by real cost runs, which the PR defers. Are they safe defaults?

asks: Do the limits change for normal Turns?

chapters.caption: Version status, failure reason, and summed cost show whether generations work.
chapters.body: GET /api/walkthroughs/:id returns status, failure reason, and cost summed from the generation Conversation's cost_usd metric rows, and returns 404 if the source turns private [1][2]. After enabling experimental.walkthroughs, watch ready versus failed rows and their cost; a Turn that ends without a Walkthrough shows as failed [3].

decisions.question: No metric or log counts ready versus failed versions or reaper timeouts; outcomes show only in version rows.

asks: How do we know generations succeed in production?
